name: libfiber (iqiyi)
workload: TCP echo server IOPS at 100/200/500/1000 concurrent connections, libfiber sample vs libmill, Go and libco samples.
claimed_speedup: Bar chart only (values read from the image, approximate): at 100 concurrency libfiber ~232k QPS vs libco ~147k, libmill ~201k, golang ~155k; at 1000 concurrency ~178k vs libco ~106k (derived from chart, no numeric table on page)
tradeoffs: LGPL-3.0. Hooks libc network APIs on Unix so blocking drivers become coroutine-friendly; runs event loops (epoll, io_uring, iocp). C API with C++ wrappers.
caveats: First-party chart only; the page gives no CPU, OS, compiler or flags and no numbers other than the picture. Benchmark sources for libco and libmill are in the repo benchmark directory but were not opened. Measures network echo IOPS, not raw context switch cost.
found_via: WebSearch 'github C++ fiber library faster than boost.context or libco benchmark README'

name: libgo
workload: Context switch overhead at 1, 1000 and 30000 coroutines, measured by a third party (libcopp author) in a gist across libcopp, libco, libgo, ucontext and goroutines.
claimed_speedup: 30 ns vs libco 84 ns at 1 coroutine; 32 ns vs 168 ns at 1000; 150 ns vs 450 ns at 30000; ucontext 439/505/890 ns (gist table, Sept 2019). Fastest row in that gist apart from C++20 stackless coroutines
compiler_and_flags: -O2 -DNDEBUG (per gist notes); compiler versions not confirmed
tradeoffs: Full multi-thread scheduler, channels, hooks of libc blocking calls; heavier than a bare context switch library. Uses boost.context internally in newer versions.
caveats: Gist is written by a competing library author, CPU not stated, comments dispute methodology and note old libgo used ucontext. libgo's own README compares only against Go (switch cost graphs on a 2018 MacBook, images only). Boost.Context itself was not a column.
found_via: WebSearch 'stackful coroutine library C benchmark boost.context libco ucontext ns per switch' -> owent gist

name: libcopp
workload: Context switch overhead at 1, 1000 and 30000 coroutines (author's gist); CI output also publishes a benchmark report.
claimed_speedup: libcopp 77/105/273 ns vs libco (static stack pool) 84/168/450 ns vs ucontext 439/505/890 ns at 1/1000/30000 coroutines (gist table, Sept 2019); 1.1x at 1 coroutine, 1.6x at 1000, 1.65x at 30000 vs libco (derived from page data)
license: MIT and BSL-1.0 (dual per repo page)
tradeoffs: Offers stackful (boost.context based fcontext) and C++20 stackless coroutines, stack pools, task layer.
caveats: First-party gist from 2019, CPU not stated; libgo is faster than libcopp in the same table. Gain over libco at 1 coroutine is only 9 percent. Latest numbers live in GitHub Actions CI output which was not opened.
found_via: WebSearch 'stackful coroutine library C benchmark ... libco ucontext' -> 'coroutine benckmark' gist; vcpkg ports search

name: minicoro
workload: CPU cycles per context switch, initialize and uninitialize on x86_64 with pre-allocated coroutines, assembly method vs ucontext and Windows fibers.
claimed_speedup: Linux x86_64 switch: assembly 9 cycles vs ucontext 352 cycles (about 39x); init 31 vs 383 cycles; Windows assembly 33 cycles vs fibers 69
tradeoffs: Single-header C; asymmetric coroutines; fixed fallbacks to ucontext/fibers on other platforms (ucontext on macOS, ARM, RISC-V).
caveats: Baseline is its own ucontext fallback, not Boost.Context or libco; compiler and flags not stated. Public-domain dedication: no patent grant. An independent issue on ucoro (a minicoro derivative) shows Boost.Context at ~6 ns per round trip, so minicoro is not shown to beat Boost.Context.
found_via: WebSearch 'vcpkg coroutine fiber library stackful context switch nanoseconds'

name: libaco
workload: Context switch between coroutines (standalone stack) and memory per coroutine with 10,000,000 coroutines, on AWS c5d.large.
claimed_speedup: 10.29 ns per switch (shared FPU env) / 10.38 ns (own FPU env); 2.8 GB for 10M coroutines with 120 B copy stacks. README claims 'fastest' context switch complying with Sys V ABI; no table against libco on the page
compiler_and_flags: gcc -g -O2 (build lines in README); benchmark binary built via make.sh with tcmalloc preload
tradeoffs: Asymmetric coroutines only, x86 and x86-64 Sys V only, shared-stack copy design, one instance per thread.
caveats: The page names no measured baseline numbers: it only argues that libco has an ABI bug (stack pointer used to address heap memory). Direct comparison to libco or Boost.Context is not shown, so qualification is weak. Verifier should run or locate a head-to-head.
found_via: WebSearch 'fast C coroutine library benchmark context switch faster than libco boost.context' -> HN 'Libaco' thread

name: libdill
workload: Coroutine context switch and create/terminate time on i7-4770k and Core 2 Duo, libdill vs Go and gccgo.
claimed_speedup: i7 4770k: 16 ns per switch (13 ns optimized branch) vs Go 331 ns and gccgo 825 ns; create/terminate 44 ns (25 ns optimized) vs Go 237 ns and gccgo 3652 ns
tradeoffs: C structured-concurrency API with channels and I/O; signal mask handling cost; degrades past about 32k coroutines (mmap limits).
caveats: Baseline is Go, not Boost.Context/libco, and the numbers come from an issue comment by the author, with compiler flags unstated. Optimized variant was not merged as stated. Last commit date not confirmed.
found_via: WebSearch 'libdill libmill context switch benchmark nanoseconds coroutine C'
